task: Classify a public medicine-notice table column as batch, expiry, distribution or other, then preserve the original row association for date review.
selection: 60 most recently updated MHRA medicine recall/notification notices at collection time; English GOV.UK Content API; exclude unsupported table layouts with reasons.
labels: Explicit, AI-assisted annotation of source column headings; not clinical-expert annotation. No labels generated by the learned classifier or existing date-label rules.
split: Chronological 60/20/20 by document groups. Identical table payloads stay in one group; the group's newest publication date determines its position. No random row-level split.
features: Column heading text only; character-within-word TF-IDF ngrams 3 through 5. No document IDs, URLs, dates, batch values or labels as features.
model: LogisticRegression(C=1.0, class_weight=balanced, max_iter=2000, random_state=42); fixed in advance, no hyperparameter search.
abstention: Predictions below 0.60 maximum class score become unclassified; scores are not calibrated probabilities. Date values remain review candidates even above this threshold.
limitations: One regulator and many repeated headings/templates. Document holdout is not unseen-template or independent clinical validation. Report exact header overlap and an unseen-heading slice.
pdf_ocr: Three newest test documents with original PDF attachments; first two pages at 150 DPI; Tesseract eng, OEM 1, PSM 3. Compare OCR date-value coverage to corresponding HTML-table dates, not full batch-link accuracy. Never train on these PDF evaluation outputs.
